BENILLA_NUM_PET_ACTION_SLOTS = 10
-- The token textures, quoted verbatim from ref PetActionBarFrame.lua:6-12. They are -- GLOBALS on purpose: `GetPetActionInfo` returns the NAME of one for a token slot, and the -- paint below resolves it with getglobal, exactly as the reference does. PET_DEFENSIVE_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Defend" PET_AGGRESSIVE_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Racial_BloodRage" PET_PASSIVE_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Seal" PET_ATTACK_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_GhoulFrenzy" PET_FOLLOW_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Ability_Tracking" PET_WAIT_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Spell_Nature_TimeStop" PET_DISMISS_TEXTURE = "Interface\\Icons\\Spell_Shadow_Teleport"
-- ── The autocast sparkle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- The reference's "autocast is on" mark is a <Model> playing -- Interface\Buttons\UI-AutoCastButton.mdx, and what that model actually is came out of the -- shipped .m2 with `benilla-extract m2bones`/`m2part`: -- -- 4 bones, pivoting at the corners of a 0.02 x 0.02 unit square, each keyed with the -- SAME 5-key 2.000 s translation loop walking the square edge by edge (0.5 s per edge) — -- the four phase-shifted by one corner each, so they chase one another round it. -- 4 particle emitters, one per bone: 300/s, life 1.000 s, Add blend, unlit, texture -- Interface\Buttons\GlowStar.blp, size half-extent 0.005 -> 0.002 -> 0.001 over life, -- colour (0.976,0.875,0.192,1) -> (0.996,0.945,0.745,1) -> (1,1,1,0). Its spline has 4 -- control points ALL AT THE ORIGIN, so a particle never travels: it is born where the -- bone is and shrinks away there. The effect is therefore four comet trails running -- round the button's rim, not a rotating ring. -- -- Model units -> pixels is the same 1200 px/unit calibration BagFrame.xml derived from the -- Cooldown model (its own header carries the derivation), and it CROSS-CHECKS here: the -- lap square is 0.02 units, the ref's Model carries scale="1.2", and 0.02 * 1200 * 1.2 = -- 28.8 px — the rim of a 30 px button, which is where the sparkles visibly run. That -- agreement between two independently-authored UI models is the reason to trust the -- number rather than eyeball a size. -- -- OUR ONE DEPARTURE is the particle COUNT: 300 live per emitter is 12 000 quads across a -- full bar, for a trail that reads identically at a fraction of that. We draw -- BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_TRAIL per emitter, evenly spaced in AGE, which samples the same -- position/size/colour ramps at the same times — the trail's shape, speed and colour are -- the file's; only its density is ours. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT = 1200 BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE = 1.2 -- the ref Model's BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD = 2.0 -- seq0 loop, seconds BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_LIFE = 1.0 -- particle lifespan BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_TRAIL = 8 -- ours (see above) BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_EMITTERS = 4 -- 0.02 units square, in pixels. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SIZE = 0.02 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE -- Half-extent -> full width, in pixels: {0.005, 0.002, 0.001} * 2 * K * scale. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_STAR = { 0.010 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE, 0.004 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE, 0.002 * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PX_PER_UNIT * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SCALE, } -- The over-life colour ramp's three keys (the file's), as {r, g, b, a}. BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_COLOR = { {0.976, 0.875, 0.192, 1.0}, {0.996, 0.945, 0.745, 1.0}, {1.000, 1.000, 1.000, 0.0}, }
-- Where an emitter sits at lap fraction `f` (0..1), as an offset from the button's CENTER -- in pixels. The bone tracks walk the square anticlockwise from its bottom-left corner, -- one edge per quarter-lap; this is that walk, re-centred (the model's square runs 0..0.02 -- in both axes, so its centre is at 0.01). function BenillaPetAutocast_Point(f) local h = BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_SIZE / 2 f = f - math.floor(f) -- wrap into 0..1 local edge = f * 4 local leg = math.floor(edge) local t = edge - leg -- 0..1 along this edge if leg == 0 then return -h, -h + t * 2 * h -- bottom-left -> top-left elseif leg == 1 then return -h + t * 2 * h, h -- top-left -> top-right elseif leg == 2 then return h, h - t * 2 * h -- top-right -> bottom-right else return h - t * 2 * h, -h -- bottom-right -> bottom-left end end
-- Sample a 3-key over-life ramp (the M2's own {k0, k1 at mid, k2} shape, linear between). function BenillaPetAutocast_Ramp(keys, age) local a, b, t if age <= 0.5 then a, b, t = keys[1], keys[2], age * 2 else a, b, t = keys[2], keys[3], (age - 0.5) * 2 end if type(a) == "number" then return a + (b - a) * t end local out = {} for i = 1, table.getn(a) do out[i] = a[i] + (b[i] - a[i]) * t end return out end
-- Build one button's sparkle pool: EMITTERS x TRAIL textures, hidden until autocast is on. function BenillaPetAutocast_Create(button) button.sparks = {} for i = 1, BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_EMITTERS * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_TRAIL do local t = button:CreateTexture(nil, "OVERLAY") t:SetTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\GlowStar") t:SetBlendMode("ADD") t:Hide() table.insert(button.sparks, t) end end
-- Advance one button's sparkles to the bar's shared clock. Shared on purpose: the four -- emitters are one model, and every autocasting button plays the same loop in step, which -- is what the reference's per-button Models do too (each starts at sequence time 0 and -- they never drift, the loop being exact). function BenillaPetAutocast_Update(button, clock) if not button.sparks then return end if not button.autocasting then for i = 1, table.getn(button.sparks) do button.sparks[i]:Hide() end return end local n = 1 for e = 0, BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_EMITTERS - 1 do -- The four bones are the same lap, a quarter apart. local phase = clock / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD + e / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_EMITTERS for k = 0, BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_TRAIL - 1 do -- Evenly spaced in AGE: this star was emitted `age` seconds ago, so it sits -- where the bone was then and has aged that far along the ramps. local age = (k / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_TRAIL) * BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_LIFE local x, y = BenillaPetAutocast_Point(phase - age / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD) local life = age / BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_LIFE local size = BenillaPetAutocast_Ramp(BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_STAR, life) local c = BenillaPetAutocast_Ramp(BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_COLOR, life) local spark = button.sparks[n] n = n + 1 spark:SetWidth(size) spark:SetHeight(size) spark:ClearAllPoints() spark:SetPoint("CENTER", button, "CENTER", x, y) spark:SetVertexColor(c[1], c[2], c[3]) spark:SetAlpha(c[4]) spark:Show() end end end
-- ── The buttons ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
function BenillaPetActionButton_OnLoad(button, index) -- Ref PetActionButton_OnLoad l.234-235. The right-click registration is load-bearing, -- not boilerplate: it is the whole autocast toggle, and without it a right click is -- simply never delivered. button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- The drag trio (decision 1010). Both buttons drag, ref-verbatim -- (PetActionButton_OnLoad l.234) — and unlike the action bar's, ALL THREE gestures here -- reach the same verb: the reference's OnClick-under-shift, OnDragStart and -- OnReceiveDrag all call PickupPetAction, which forks on whether the cursor is already -- carrying. LOCK_ACTIONBAR stays the vanilla default (unlocked), so — as on ActionBar -- — the ref's cvar guard is not reproduced and the drag is always live. button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton", "RightButton") button.index = index button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.cooldown = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown") button.autocastable = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "AutoCastable") BenillaPetAutocast_Create(button) end
-- Ref PetActionButton_OnClick. The CheckButton widget toggles itself BEFORE OnClick fires, -- and the reference immediately clears that (`this:SetChecked(0)`) — nothing about this bar -- is locally latched, because the server owns every bit of it. Left = run the slot, unless -- the pet is already on the attack, in which case it calls off; right = flip autocast. function BenillaPetActionButton_OnClick(button, mouseButton) button:SetChecked(0) -- Shift outranks the button fork entirely (ref l.253-255): a shift-click on the pet bar -- is a pick-up whichever mouse button it came from, and it never toggles autocast. if IsShiftKeyDown() then PickupPetAction(button.index) BenillaPetActionBar_Update() elseif mouseButton == "RightButton" then TogglePetAutocast(button.index) elseif IsPetAttackActive(button.index) then PetStopAttack() else CastPetAction(button.index) end end
-- Both drag ends are the SAME verb (ref l.269-283, byte-verified at `0x4be180`): with an -- empty cursor it picks the slot up, with a pet payload already held it drops onto this -- slot. There is no separate "place" binding on this bar, which is also why a spell or an -- item can never land here — nothing but a pet slot produces the payload it accepts. function BenillaPetActionButton_OnDragStart(button) PickupPetAction(button.index) BenillaPetActionBar_Update() end
function BenillaPetActionButton_OnReceiveDrag(button) PickupPetAction(button.index) BenillaPetActionBar_Update() end
-- Ref PetActionButton_OnEnter. A token slot has no spell to look up, so its tooltip is -- built from the two strings the info call already returned (the ref's own `isToken` fork); -- a spell slot goes through the engine's tooltip channel. function BenillaPetActionButton_OnEnter(button) if not GameTooltip then return end -- engine tests load file subsets if not button.tooltipName then return end GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor(GameTooltip, button) if button.isToken then GameTooltip:SetText(button.tooltipName, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) if button.tooltipSubtext then GameTooltip:AddLine(button.tooltipSubtext, "", 0.5, 0.5, 0.5) end GameTooltip:Show() else GameTooltip:SetPetAction(button.index) end end
function BenillaPetActionButton_OnLeave(button) if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:Hide() end end
-- ── The bar ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Ref PetActionBar_Update + PetActionBar_UpdateCooldowns, fused (one refresh event, see the -- header). Every branch below is the reference's, including the two that are easy to lose: -- an unnamed slot HIDES its button, and a slot with no texture swaps the button's ring from -- the filled UI-Quickslot2 to the empty UI-Quickslot. function BenillaPetActionBar_Update() local usable = GetPetActionsUsable() for i = 1, BENILLA_NUM_PET_ACTION_SLOTS do local button = getglobal("BenillaPetActionButton" .. i) local name, subtext, texture, isToken, isActive, autoCastAllowed, autoCastEnabled = GetPetActionInfo(i) button.isToken = isToken button.tooltipSubtext = subtext if isToken then -- The token convention: what came back are the NAMES of globals. button.icon:SetTexture(getglobal(texture)) button.tooltipName = getglobal(name) else button.icon:SetTexture(texture) button.tooltipName = name end
if isActive then button:SetChecked(1) else button:SetChecked(0) end if autoCastAllowed then button.autocastable:Show() else button.autocastable:Hide() end button.autocasting = autoCastEnabled
-- An unnamed slot hides — UNLESS the drop grid is up, which is the whole point of -- the grid: while a pet action rides the cursor every slot shows, so you can see -- where it may land (ref PetActionBar_Update l.122-128 + PetActionBar_ShowGrid). if name or (BenillaPetActionBarFrame.showgrid or 0) > 0 then button:Show() else button:Hide() end
if texture then SetDesaturation(button.icon, not usable and 1 or nil) button.icon:Show() button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-Quickslot2") else button.icon:Hide() button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-Quickslot") end
local start, duration, enable = GetPetActionCooldown(i) CooldownFrame_SetTimer(button.cooldown, start, duration, enable) end end
function BenillaPetActionBar_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") frame:RegisterEvent("PET_BAR_UPDATE") -- The drop grid (decision 1010). A counter rather than a flag, ref-verbatim -- (PetActionBar_ShowGrid/_HideGrid): our engine derives the pair off one payload edge -- so they strictly alternate, but the counter is what the reference keeps and it costs -- nothing to keep it too. frame:RegisterEvent("PET_BAR_SHOWGRID") frame:RegisterEvent("PET_BAR_HIDEGRID") frame.showgrid = 0 frame.clock = 0 BenillaPetActionBar_OnEvent(frame) end
-- The bar exists exactly while PetHasActionBar() does. Its show/hide re-fires the managed -- bottom-stack pass (UIParent.xml, decision 0272) — the pet term of that stack is what -- lifts the cast bar and the chat frame clear of it, which is the ref's own -- PetActionBarFrame.xml:205-210. function BenillaPetActionBar_OnEvent(frame, eventName) if eventName == "PET_BAR_SHOWGRID" then frame.showgrid = frame.showgrid + 1 elseif eventName == "PET_BAR_HIDEGRID" and frame.showgrid > 0 then frame.showgrid = frame.showgrid - 1 end if PetHasActionBar() then BenillaPetActionBar_Update() frame:Show() else frame:Hide() end end
-- The shared sparkle clock. One OnUpdate for the whole bar rather than ten: the four -- emitters are one looping model, so every autocasting button is in step by construction. function BenillaPetActionBar_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) frame.clock = (frame.clock or 0) + elapsed if frame.clock > BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD then frame.clock = frame.clock - BENILLA_PET_AUTOCAST_PERIOD end for i = 1, BENILLA_NUM_PET_ACTION_SLOTS do BenillaPetAutocast_Update(getglobal("BenillaPetActionButton" .. i), frame.clock) end end
